inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q3 2026 10-Q weighted-average shares assuming dilution (284.6 basic + 0.7 options/RSUs). Held FLAT because SBC (plus equity-award withholding) is fully expensed in the flows; ITW's ~$1.5B/yr buybacks fund far more than the flat count and are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation expense $69M (ITW_Annual_FY2025.txt:3138). ITW publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure and no separate net-share-settlement tax line; financing 'Other, net' of $(32)M (line 3209), which carries award tax withholding, is added as an upper-bound proxy -> $101M.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity ~9.2% (10y UST ~4.3%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.98 for a diversified US industrial); after-tax cost of debt ~3.3% (mostly fixed-rate USD/EUR notes, 24% tax); market weights ~89% equity ($80B cap) / ~11% debt ($9.4B) -> ~8.6%, used as 8.5% in all three scenarios. Risk is charged once through the scenario weights, not via per-scenario WACC.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A: operating-lease cost (~$90M/yr) is already inside reported operating income and hence inside the EBITDA margin path; operating lease liabilities ($242M at FY2025) are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is immaterial (<$5M); no bridge item.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md as a US operating company (diversified industrial, cyclical end markets: auto builds, industrial capex, food service, residential renovation); not a bank/REIT/holdco/LIC. First valuation of ITW -- no prior DCF and no memory entry. FY0 is FY2025 (revenue $16,044M, operating income $4,216M = 26.3%, D&A $397M = depreciation 317 + amortization 80, capex $419M). Adj. EBITDA margin in the paths is pre-SBC (operating income + D&A + SBC): FY2025 29.2%. Year 1 (FY2026) anchored to Q3-2026 guidance (Oct 27, 2026): revenue +4.5-5.5% (9M actual +5.0%), operating margin 26.5-27.5% -> 27.0% + D&A 2.4% + SBC 0.45% = 29.9% adj. EBITDA. Interest income ($40M FY2025) NOT stripped: ITW carries ~$8.6B net debt, so no net-cash double count arises. Net debt at 30 Sep 2026: total debt $9,372M (short-term $2,219M incl. commercial paper and Nov-2026 notes + long-term $7,153M) less cash $809M. Working capital capture negative (-15% of the revenue change): receivables + inventory (~$4.8B) far exceed payables, so growth consumes cash (9M 2026: receivables -$300M, inventories -$174M). Pension plans are modestly funded and not bridged. Buyback pace: $1.5B/yr FY2023-25, $1.31B in 9M 2026 (guide ~$1.5B); the flat count is therefore funded, not a convention. Cash tax 24% of EBIT: FY2025 cash taxes paid $1,052M vs book ETR 22.7%; FY2026 ETR guide 23-24% excluding discrete benefits.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue path anchored to management's 4%+ through-cycle organic target discounted for a decade of ~1-2% delivered organic growth (FY2023-25 organic roughly flat); equity CAGR rejected as a growth signal because ITW returns ~100% of FCF via dividends and buybacks, holding book value near $3B.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.3% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS (9.6% 5yr) and revenue (5.0% 5yr). Book value is held flat by design (~$2.9B/yr of dividends + buybacks), so it is not a valid growth proxy here.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (FY2020 2,529; FY2022 1,873; FY2025 2,638). The 3-year FCF CAGR (12.1%) starts from a FY2022 trough depressed by an inventory build (OCF 2,348) and overstates trend; the 5-year (0.9%) is the more honest read. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are near-identical: SBC is ~0.4% of revenue and is not absorbing growth. The 5-year revenue and EPS CAGRs start from the COVID trough FY2020 and overstate trend; the 3-year revenue CAGR of 0.2% reflects flat organic growth plus product-line simplification.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands on guidance (+5% revenue, ~27% operating margin). Organic growth settles at ~3-3.5% (below management's 4%+ target, above the FY2023-25 run-rate) as T&M/Electronics and Welding capex recovery offsets Construction and Automotive EU/China drags. 80/20 enterprise initiatives add ~30-40bps/yr of operating margin to ~28.5% by FY2030, then plateau.

bull.narrative: The industrial capex upturn broadens from T&M/Electronics and Welding (mid-to-high-teens organic in Q3 2026) to the whole portfolio; Customer-Back Innovation finally delivers the 4%+ organic target plus ~1pt of bolt-on M&A; China auto share gains with domestic EV OEMs more than offset foreign-OEM declines. Operating margin reaches management's 30% ambition by FY2030 and holds.

bear.narrative: PMI and industrial capex plateau as JPMorgan and others warn, tipping into a 2027 industrial recession (revenue -3%, comparable to ITW's 2020 dip but milder); Construction Products stays weak on North American renovation, tariff volatility hits China-exposed Auto and T&M demand, and organic growth reverts to the ~1-2% of FY2023-25. Margin deleverage in 2027 (operating margin ~25%) is only partly recovered; 80/20 gains are exhausted near 26.5-27% operating margin.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance year delivered; ~3-3.5% organic growth (between delivered history and the 4%+ target) and 80/20-driven margin expansion to ~28.5% operating margin by FY2030, then mature. Cash conversion ~100% of net income, buybacks keep the share count falling faster than the flat-count assumption.
scenario_narratives.bull: Capex-cycle recovery broadens across segments, CBI delivers 4%+ organic plus bolt-ons, and the 30% operating-margin ambition is met by FY2030; the market keeps paying a premium multiple for best-in-class returns.
scenario_narratives.bear: Industrial capex plateau becomes a 2027 downturn; Construction, Automotive Europe/China and tariff uncertainty keep organic growth at ~1-2%; margin expansion stalls near 27% operating margin and the terminal multiple compresses to 15x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 20% from the 15% default because ITW is a short-cycle industrial at a cycle-mature point (PMI/capex plateau flagged by brokers) with three segments already in organic decline, though its balance sheet carries no solvency risk. Base 55% because the guidance year is nearly complete and the base path sits between delivered and targeted organic growth. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- a broad capex upturn, CBI hitting 4%+ organic after a decade of misses, and the 30% margin target.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ITW is a mature, high-return compounder whose value rests on margin durability and cash conversion rather than growth. The model expenses SBC (plus award withholding), holds the diluted count flat, builds FCF from components with working capital consuming cash on growth, and caps the terminal multiple at 18x (15x bear) for a cyclical industrial.
key_risks_to_valuation: Organic growth: every 1pt of sustained revenue growth moves value materially; ITW has missed its 4%+ organic target for years.
Margin plateau: base assumes ~150bps more operating margin from 80/20; if enterprise initiatives are exhausted near 27%, value falls toward the bear case.
Industrial cycle: short-cycle exposure (Welding, T&M, Auto) can cut revenue 5-15% in a downturn (2009: -21%, 2020: -11%).
Terminal dependence: with WACC 8.5% and g 2.5%, roughly three-quarters of base value sits in the terminal value.
Tariffs and FX: tariff-policy volatility and USD translation affect reported revenue and China-exposed segments.
